transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-12 09:00 PT / 17:00 UTC - Ops Reset and Focus Huddle - duration ~52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (host), Jonas, Priya, Liam, Aisha, Ravi, Evan + all-hands.
--- Summary / TL;DR (auto): Q1 priorities: stabilize SLOs, Dedicated ramp, Redwood Private onboarding, cost levers.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, um, thanks for joining. quick housekeeping — we'll keep this to about 50 minutes, then open for Q&A. um, first slide is.. uh, the high level ask: focus.
[00:18] Maya Chen: last quarter was, uh, lots of wins, but also some noise on latency spikes and cost. we need a tighter plan for product ops.
[00:34] Jonas Rivera: yeah, we saw a couple of outlier clusters causing 95th percentile blips — some of that is GC and some kv cache churn with long sequences. kubernetes autoscaler mis-routed a few pods, sorry cube-er-netes, bad transcription there, but you know what i mean.
[00:50] Priya Singh: to add, our roadmap drifted with too many concurrent experiments. Q1 we cut to the three bets: 1) latency and reliability, 2) Dedicated capacity stabilization, 3) Private onboarding acceleration.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: operationally, that means freeze non-critical infra changes, tighten CI gating for runtime kernel swaps, and hold off broad quantization experiments until we validate perf on canaries.
[01:28] Audience: (background chatter)
[01:35] Maya Chen: quick people note — hiring pace is going to be conservative for the quarter, we still prioritize critical eng, sales for committed deals, and a few research roles. aisha will speak to that.
[01:50] Aisha Gomez: yep. we are pausing some requisitions, reprioritizing senior infra and se hires. we'll share a public-ish doc with rationale and impacted teams. this is not a mass hiring freeze, but targeted.
[02:06] Ravi Patel: from GTM, pipeline looks healthy but conversion timelines have slipped for some large accounts — Dedicated procurement and private VPC requirements are longer than expected, legal reviews, SAML, KMS keys, ok?
[02:24] Maya Chen: ok, so let's walk through the bets. priya?
[02:29] Priya Singh: first, latency and reliability. goal: 95th <= 220ms on our hosted LLM endpoints for the top 5% of common seq lengths; reduce incidence of KV cache thrash. we will put in place a latency SLO runbook.
[02:45] Jonas Rivera: the root causes are twofold: kernel choice for certain transformer variants, and upstream autoscaling policies. our short-term mitigations: pin kernel versions in prod for the next two weeks, and adjust autoscaler thresholds to avoid oscillation.
[03:01] Liam O'Connor: and continuous batching tweaks — we'll enable smaller max batch sizes for low-latency tiers while allowing higher batching for cost-optimized tiers. that's part of the canary config.
[03:18] Maya Chen: are there realistic customer-visible regressions from pinning kernels?
[03:22] Jonas Rivera: small risk for certain long-tail models; we'll keep a rollback path. the canary will run on 5% of traffic.
[03:31] Priya Singh: acceptance criteria: real-time telemetry shows 10% reduction in 95th within two weeks on canaries.
[03:39] Audience member 1: so is this a hosted-only change or Dedicated as well?
[03:43] Liam O'Connor: both — but Dedicated customers can opt-in to pinned kernels; default will be compatibility-first.
[03:51] [04:00] Priya Singh: second bet, Dedicated capacity commitments. we need to hit utilization targets for reserved pools and reduce oversubscription for burst capacity. jonas?
[04:10] Jonas Rivera: we're projecting ramp to 60% baseline utilization on reserved GPU pools by March, which will help unit economics. action here is to tighten routing policies and prioritize committed customer traffic.
[04:23] Ravi Patel: for sales, we need clearer messaging on guaranteed throughput vs best-effort burst — customers ask about SLA, S L A fine grain. we'll publish a short doc for sales.
[04:37] Maya Chen: third bet, Redwood Private/VPC onboarding. timeline — we have three pilots in pipeline, two legal reviews in progress. 
[04:47] Evan Moore: technical blockers are mostly onboarding automation — network templates, KMS/HSM integration steps and audit-log retention defaults. we will provide a one-click VPC template for partners. some of that is already in docs but messy.
[05:06] Audience: (crosstalk)
[05:12] Maya Chen: quick finance note — cost targets: reduce hosted per-token egress costs by 8% via batching and cache hit improvements. we can't sacrifice latency for cost savings unless it's opt-in.
[05:26] Priya Singh: that means offering two profiles: low-latency and cost-optimized, and defaulting new users to low-latency.
[05:34] Liam O'Connor: technical approach: prefix caching for chat, hotspot KV cache tuning, intelligent batching based on workload classification.
[05:46] Jonas Rivera: also quantization guidance — don't bulk roll quantization across-prod; tiered experiments with evals and quality monitoring.
[05:58] Maya Chen: ok, questions. please keep to two.
[06:05] Audience Q1 (Engineering): for the latency SLO runbook, who owns the canary and rollback?
[06:12] Liam O'Connor: engops will own canary execution, se ops will monitor customer-facing metrics, and platform reliability will own rollback criteria.
[06:21] Audience Q2 (Sales): how are we prioritizing Dedicated vs Private on sales incentives?
[06:27] Ravi Patel: quota motion is prioritized for committed reserved agreements this quarter; Private pilots get additional AE/SE support credits.
[06:34] Audience Q3 (Product): what about roadmap scope changes for the SDKs?
[06:37] Priya Singh: SDKs get stabilized patches, major API changes are postponed to Q2 unless critical.
[06:44] [06:50] Maya Chen: on hiring — aisha, can you outline priority levels?
[06:54] Aisha Gomez: level 1: critical infra, se for pilots, and a few sales motions; level 2: product roles that unblock roadmap; level 3: growth/ops are mostly paused. we'll be explicit in the doc.
[07:10] Audience: uh-huh
[07:16] Priya Singh: small product update — we'll defer some new UI experiments, but rolling out the new route-based tracing dashboard mid-February for observability. it's important for debugging SLOs.
[07:29] Jonas Rivera: on observability, we will add token-level latency attribution to the console so PMs and SEs can see where cost is coming from.
[07:40] Audience Q4 (Support): can we get an SLA runbook for SOC compliance checks?
[07:45] Jonas Rivera: yes, we'll include auditable steps for SOC 2 and ISO proofs — SAML, KMS, and audit logs mapping.
[07:54] [08:00] Maya Chen: ok, lightning round — five updates, 30 seconds each.
[08:03] Liam O'Connor: infra: freeze non-essential infra merges for two weeks; fast path only for critical bugfixes.
[08:12] Priya Singh: product: publish pared-down roadmap and highlight the three bets by next Monday.
[08:18] Jonas Rivera: runtime: pin kernels for canary, prepare rollback plan.
[08:24] Ravi Patel: sales: share top 10 enterprise accounts and procurement blockers.
[08:30] Aisha Gomez: people: hiring priority doc and interview calibration guidance.
[08:36] [08:40] Maya Chen: open mic — quick Q&A.
[08:44] Audience Q5 (Engineer): are we deprecating older model variants?
[08:50] Priya Singh: some older, unsupported variants will be deprecated in phases; we'll notify impacted customers and provide migration tooling.
[08:59] Audience Q6 (SE): private onboarding automation ETA?
[09:04] Evan Moore: base templates in two weeks, full automation in six to eight weeks pending pilot feedback.
[09:12] [09:20] Audience (Finance): what's the target for cost savings this quarter?
[09:24] Maya Chen: 8% unit cost reduction with a path to 12% if pilots show strong cache hit improvements.
[09:31] [09:40] Priya Singh: final note — we measure success by improved latency SLOs, Dedicated utilization up, and clean Private pilots.
[09:49] Liam O'Connor: and by reduced operational incidents month-over-month.
[09:56] Maya Chen: thank you. we'll post the deck, the prioritized hiring doc, the SLO runbook draft and the canary checklist. any other hand-raises?
[10:10] (silence)
[10:18] Maya Chen: ok, meeting adjourned — thanks everyone.

--- End of transcript. Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear of "KV cache" as "K V cash", "Kubernetes" as "cube-er-netes". Some speaker labels generalized.
